name: Gao PAE versus TURP
question: How do prostatic arterial embolization and TURP compare for symptoms, urinary function, and complications in men with BPH?

design.population: 114 men with BPH, IPSS greater than 7 after failed medical therapy, prostate volume 20–100 mL, and peak flow below 15 mL/s were randomized to PAE or TURP.
design.description: Prospective randomized controlled comparative trial; powered to detect a 3-point IPSS difference; no primary endpoint expressly designated; modified intention-to-treat analysis
design.locator: Full text, Study Population and Study Design, p 921

verdictNote: Both improved function; TURP improved early outcomes more, while PAE had more complications and shorter hospital stays.
takeaway: In 114 men randomized to prostatic arterial embolization or TURP, both arms improved through 24 months. TURP improved symptoms and flow more at 1 and 3 months; PAE had more adverse events or complications, including technical and clinical failures (30/57 vs 17/57), but shorter stays.

reports.label: Primary randomized report
reports.citation: Gao YA, Huang Y, Zhang R, et al. "Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Prostatic Arterial Embolization versus Transurethral Resection of the Prostate—A Prospective, Randomized, and Controlled Clinical Trial." *Radiology.* 2014;270(3):920-928. doi:10.1148/radiol.13122803
reports.followUp: Assessments scheduled at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months; mean follow-up 22.5 months; five patients lost by 12 months
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Outcome Assessment, p 923; Results, p 924

results.endpoint: IPSS, quality of life, peak flow, and postvoid residual
results.measure: Change from baseline at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months

values.exp: Improved at all visits; comparable to TURP at 12 and 24 months
values.ctl: Improved at all visits; greater improvement than PAE at 1 and 3 months

results.note: Within-group P = .001; the study was powered for a 3-point IPSS difference but did not designate a primary endpoint. Arm means and confidence intervals were not tabulated.
results.locator: Full text, Study Design, p 921; Functional Results and Figure 5, pp 925, 927

results.measure: Between-group comparative reduction at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months
results.note: Both arms improved from baseline (P = .001); numerical arm means and confidence intervals were not tabulated.
results.locator: Full text, Functional Results, p 925; Figure 6, p 928

results.measure: Clinical failure through 24 months in treated patients
results.note: Failure meant IPSS decrease ≤25%, IPSS ≥18, QOL decrease ≤1, and QOL ≥4 and/or flow increase <2.5 mL/s with peak flow ≤7 mL/s; TURP followed at six months for clinical failures. The paper's reported percentages do not reconcile with the stated treated denominators.
results.locator: Full text, Outcome Assessment, p 923; Results, p 924; Table 3, p 926

harms.label: Overall adverse events and complications
harms.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Discussion, pp 925–926
harms.note: P = .029; totals include technical and clinical failures.

harms.label: Clavien I–II and III–IV adverse events or complications
harms.note: P = .113 for minor and .275 for major events; PAE major events were three technical and five clinical failures.

harms.label: Blood transfusion and transurethral resection syndrome
harms.note: Transfusion was Clavien II; resection syndrome was Clavien IVb.

delivery.label: Technical success
delivery.locator: Full text, Outcome Assessment, p 923; Results, p 924
delivery.note: PAE success required selective prostatic arterial catheterization and embolization on at least one side.

delivery.label: Technical failure after PAE
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 924; Table 3, p 926
delivery.note: Bilateral iliac arterial tortuosity and atherosclerosis prevented PAE; failures underwent TURP.

delivery.label: Procedure technique

values.exp: Local anesthesia; right femoral access; 355–500 µm polyvinyl alcohol particles to stasis; bilateral 48/57 (84.2%), unilateral 6/57 (10.5%)
values.ctl: Epidural anesthesia; bipolar TURP with 26-F resectoscope; 22-F three-way Foley and saline irrigation

delivery.locator: Full text, TURP and PAE Technique, p 922; Results, p 924
delivery.note: PAE ended at complete stasis without reflux; TURP irrigation continued for at least 24 hours.

delivery.label: Procedure time, catheterization, and hospital stay
delivery.note: P = .066 for procedure time; P < .001 for catheterization, admission, and hospital stay.
